items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: In fact, that’s where I saw Dizzy, about the same thing, because his band was staying in the same hotel we were during that time

ctx.x: you don’t even have too much of dealing with the law of permutation. In other words, to make do with what you’ve got. That’s why I’ll get back to the theory of expedience. In other words you’ll find out — and naturally, you make do with what you’ve got. All of a sudden you get sensitized and you know which is poison and which isn’t. Because you’ve got to eat. Well how did you survive? Well I ate bugs, I ate this bug and I ate that bug, and then I ate this one and it made me sick so I know not to mess with that…

Well they did, they had this big apartment building in New York City for musicians that retired and stuff. And Dizzy Gillespie I think had this hospital set up where he could go and get treatments or something, down in New Jersey somewhere. But that’s sort of like what I’m speaking of. Because that we speak a different language. And so when we get put out to pasture, we should be around people that have done what we have done.
